results.question: If I cite ChatGPT, does that make an entirely AI-written assignment acceptable?
results.expected_answer: No; citation alone does not authorize circumventing assessment, passing off entire generated work, or prompts contrary to good practice and assignment rules.
results.answer:
An entirely AI-written assignment is not acceptable, because generative AI tools should never be the only source of information used [S6], and "Generative AI should not be used for the automated submission of research work, assignments, or any other academic assessments" [S3]. Furthermore, all submissions must be the original work of the researchers [S3], and none of the content generated by AI should be used in submitted work unless it is quoted and referenced as such [S6].

**Related conditions and exceptions from the retrieved sources:**

> Using Generative AI/AI tools for research and in the preparation of work does not require citation, similar to how an initial Google search for information does not require citation. Before the introduction of Generative AI, students were not required to reference web searches, sources that had not directly informed their submitted work, or the use of spell checkers. Therefore, the use of Generative AI for similar purposes need not be referenced unless an assignment brief specifically states otherwise. [S1]

> Additionally, students must include images of the prompts they used with the Generative AI tool to ensure transparency and proper attribution. [S2]

> However, students must critically evaluate any content generated using AI. [S1]
